# DESIGN.md — Pooch Professional Grooming Services - Altona North

archetype: nursery-gentle
rationale: Pet owners leaving their dog here — especially nervous, elderly or first-time-groom dogs — arrive with the same emotional stakes as a parent dropping a child at childcare; the design must answer "are these people safe and kind?" before it sells anything, and nursery-gentle's reassurance-first warmth, rounded type, and soft brand-hue grounds are exactly the right instrument for that.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [warm, reassuring, capable, unpretentious]

typography:
  display: "Plus Jakarta Sans"
  body: "Plus Jakarta Sans"
  scale: 1.25
  notes: >
    Plus Jakarta Sans is the brand-specified heading font and carries the whole personality — its
    rounded terminals read as friendly without tipping into childish. Display headings at 700 weight,
    set large (3rem–4rem on desktop). Section eyebrows in 500 weight, small-caps, 0.75rem,
    letter-spaced 0.12em. Body at 400 weight, 1.0625rem, line-height 1.7 — large enough to read
    easily on a phone in daylight. Prices set in 700 weight at 1.25rem inline with their label;
    never smaller than body. CTAs in 600 weight, never all-caps.

palette:
  primary: "#f07850"
  secondary: "#c05a30"
  accent: "#f07850"
  ground: "#fffaf7"
  surface: "#fff3ec"
  ink: "#2a1a10"
  muted: "#7a5a48"
  border: "#e8cfc0"
  application: >
    Primary (#f07850) carries the nav bar, CTA buttons, section divider bands and the hero's
    key text accent; it appears warm and lively on the near-white ground without shouting.
    Secondary (#c05a30) is used for hover states on buttons and for the pulled review quote's
    attribution line — it deepens the brand without introducing a foreign colour.
    Ground (#fffaf7) is a trace-warm off-white derived from the orange family: the whole page
    feels like a sunny kitchen rather than a clinical white space, which is exactly what "warm,
    friendly studio" asks for.
    Surface (#fff3ec) is one considered step warmer than the ground — used for the services
    section and the FAQ band so they read as raised without a border.
    Ink (#2a1a10) is the primary's darkest sibling pushed to near-black — it reads as rich
    brown-black rather than neutral, so even body copy feels like it belongs to this brand.
    Muted (#7a5a48) is a warm mid-tone that passes 4.5:1 on the ground and on the surface;
    used for descriptions, captions and secondary labels.
    Border (#e8cfc0) is a warm peachy rule — hairlines between service rows and FAQ items
    carry the palette rather than defaulting to grey.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: dominant
  card_usage: minimal
  mobile: >
    Nav collapses to a hamburger; the hero image stacks above the headline text (not behind it)
    at 16:9; the services section becomes a single column with category eyebrows as sticky
    sub-headers; the team names-list stacks vertically; the FAQ accordion stays full-width;
    the sticky booking bar appears at the bottom of the viewport on mobile only, one button,
    primary colour, sitting above the browser chrome — never over an accessibility widget corner.

composition: >
  This is a local convenience-destination hybrid: people choose it because it is nearby AND because
  they trust it with a beloved animal. The homepage has to earn both in one pass. Lead with the dogs
  — a warm, full-bleed photograph of a freshly groomed pup establishes "this is real, this is the
  result" before a word is read. Then answer the three things an anxious dog owner needs before they
  decide: are these people gentle with my dog, what does it cost, and where are they. The story
  and the team earn their place but they come after the work is shown, not before it. The full
  pricing detail belongs on the services page — the homepage carries a sample of the six core
  services with from-prices and a clear link through. Five strong reviews confirm the trust case,
  with one pulled to prominence because it names the specific thing that differentiates this salon:
  patient, reassuring care for a nervous rescue dog. The booking action is never more than one
  tap away on any screen.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Land the emotional promise immediately — a warm, friendly salon where dogs leave happy.
      The tagline and a single booking CTA. No hedging, no list of features.
    spec: >
      Full-bleed photograph of a freshly groomed dog: hero image 1790166103_62dvjh.webp, warm-lit,
      edge to edge, with a gradient overlay darkening from the lower-left third inward. Headline
      "Your dog deserves to look paw-some!" in Plus Jakarta Sans 700, 3.5rem on desktop, set in
      #fffaf7 over the lower-left quadrant of the image. A one-line standfirst beneath in warm
      near-white at 1.0625rem: "Warm, friendly grooming in Altona North — every dog leaves
      wagging." One primary-coloured button: "Book online now!" linking to the external booking URL.
      A secondary text link beside it: "See our services →" linking to services.html. Below those,
      one quiet line in 0.875rem muted: "Mon–Sat 9am–5pm · 3 Misten Avenue, Altona North." Nav
      sits above the image on the ground colour — no nav overlay on the photograph. On mobile the
      image crops to 16:9 and stacks above the text block on the ground colour; headline drops to
      2.25rem.

  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "6 of 64, chosen for range, links to services.html"
    intent: >
      Show the visitor what the salon does and what it costs before they have to ask. Six core
      services spanning the full price range (Nail Clip from $20 through De-shed from $115) give
      range without becoming a reference document. A clear "Full pricing" link makes the services
      page reachable in one click.
    spec: >
      Section on the surface colour (#fff3ec). Heading "Our grooming services" in display weight,
      left-aligned. Two columns on desktop, one on mobile. Each service as a horizontal row:
      service name in ink at 1rem 600-weight, the from-price in primary (#f07850) at 1rem
      700-weight pushed to the right of the same baseline, separated by a dotted border-colour
      leader. A one-line description in muted beneath the name. A hairline border-colour rule
      beneath each row. No per-item images, no cards, no icons, no borders around rows. The six
      items: Nail Clip (from $20), Beauty Bath (from $40), Puppy's First Trim (from $75), Bath
      & Tidy Up (from $80), Full Groom (from $105), De-shed Treatment (from $115). Below the
      six rows, one sentence in muted at 0.875rem: "Prices vary by breed, size and coat
      condition. Pensioners receive 15% off." Then an inline text link: "See full pricing for
      every breed and size →" pointing to services.html. On mobile rows stack single-column;
      the dotted leader collapses and the price sits on its own line beneath the name in primary.

  - id: gallery
    priority: supporting
    show: "6 of 8, links to gallery.html"
    intent: >
      Show the quality of the actual work from this salon. Six real results build confidence
      faster than any description. The link through rewards curiosity and drives the gallery page.
    spec: >
      A filmstrip band — six images from the gallery array in a horizontally scrollable strip,
      each image cropped to a 4:3 ratio, the rightmost image visibly cropped at the viewport edge
      to signal scrollability. Images sit flush with no border, separated only by a 4px gap on the
      ground colour — not in uniform cards. On desktop all six are visible without scrolling at a
      width that lets each image breathe. A small text link beneath the strip: "See all our work →"
      linking to gallery.html. The six images: 1790166105_wijml6.webp, 1790166106_svptvh.webp,
      1790166107_2uf8q2.webp, 1790166108_98btl5.webp, 1790166109_drmwdo.webp,
      1790166110_rvuwmy.webp.

  - id: story
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Establish that this is a family business built on genuine care, not a franchise. The owner's
      voice and the four trust commitments (no cage drying, insured, dog-safe products, free advice)
      answer the "are they safe?" question for an anxious dog owner. This section earns the booking
      decision, not just the click.
    spec: >
      Magazine-column layout on desktop: the about text in a left column at roughly 60% width, set
      at a comfortable measure (max 65ch). To its right, image 1790166109_ag71wr.webp bleeding
      slightly past the column edge at natural height. Heading "We're dog people, through and
      through" in display weight. Below the paragraph from the about section, four trust items as
      a two-column list of short lines — not icon boxes, not cards — each beginning with a
      checkmark glyph in primary and the text in ink: "Gentle handling — no cage drying, ever",
      "Premium dog-safe products only", "Fully insured, health and safety first", "Expert grooming
      advice, always free." On mobile the image moves above the text cropped to 3:2, and the trust
      list becomes single-column.

  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Five real reviews confirm that this salon is trustworthy with nervous, elderly and rescue
      dogs — exactly the reassurance an anxious owner needs. One review is given prominence because
      it names the specific thing that differentiates this salon from any other groomer.
    spec: >
      Pulled-quote treatment: Laura M's review — "They took care to reassure him and us and he had
      a wonderful time!" — set at 1.875rem Plus Jakarta Sans 400 italic, in ink, across a narrow
      centred measure (max 640px), on the ground colour. Attribution beneath in small-caps muted:
      "Laura M · Google Review." A hairline border-colour rule above and below the quote block.
      Beneath this, the remaining four reviews in a single row on desktop (two rows of two on
      tablet, stacked on mobile) — plain text columns, no borders, no graphical star elements
      (a typographic "★★★★★" in primary is acceptable), reviewer name in 600-weight ink, review
      text in body/muted, columns separated by vertical hairline rules on desktop. No avatar
      photographs — the profile photo URLs are Google-hosted and are not owned assets.

  - id: team
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Show the three real people behind every groom. No photographs are available; names, roles
      and genuine bios set typographically are warmer and more honest than silhouette placeholders,
      and the combined experience (10+ years for Irene alone) is itself a trust signal.
    spec: >
      Name-list layout on the surface colour (#fff3ec). Section heading: "The people behind the
      pampering." Three entries in a three-column row on desktop, single-column on mobile. Each
      entry: groomer's name in display weight 1.5rem ink, role in small-caps muted beneath,
      bio in body type 0.9375rem muted, max 4 lines. A short hairline border-colour rule between
      entries on desktop; a full-width rule between entries on mobile. No portrait placeholders,
      no avatar circles. The section closes with one quiet line in muted: "Each groomer certified,
      fully insured, and chosen for their genuine love of animals."

  - id: offers
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Surface the pensioner discount and the spring booking prompt. Both are real, current offers
      that can tip a visitor from considering to booking today.
    spec: >
      Highlight-band treatment: a full-width band in primary (#f07850) with ground-colour (#fffaf7)
      text. Two offers side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile. Each offer is a short block:
      offer title in 700-weight 1.25rem, no description text (none available in the content),
      no end date (none available). The pensioner offer carries a sub-line in 0.875rem: "Show your
      concession card at drop-off." No countdown timers. No urgency language beyond what the
      content itself states.

  - id: faq
    priority: supporting
    show: "6 of 11, links to booking.html for the booking question"
    intent: >
      Answer the six questions a first-time visitor is most likely to arrive with, reducing friction
      before the booking step. The accordion keeps the section scannable rather than wall-of-text.
    spec: >
      Accordion layout on the ground colour (#fffaf7). Six questions, one open at a time. Question
      text in 600-weight ink 1rem; toggle is a chevron in primary. Answer text in body/muted,
      revealed on click. A hairline border-colour rule beneath each item. The six questions: "How
      often should I get my dog groomed?", "How long will my dog's groom take?", "My dog is nervous
      about grooming — is that okay?", "What products do you use?", "What should I do before
      bringing my dog in?", "How do I book an appointment?" — the last answer includes the booking
      link and phone number. On mobile, comfortable tap targets at minimum 48px per question row.

  - id: hours_location
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Give address and hours clearly so a visitor can confirm the salon is reachable and open
      before committing. No map embed is available (coordinates null, mapEmbed empty); a clean
      typographic block is the correct and honest outcome.
    spec: >
      Stacked-band layout on the surface colour (#fff3ec). Two columns on desktop: left column
      holds the address "3 Misten Avenue, Altona North" in 700-weight ink at 1.25rem, with phone
      number "(03) 7057 0538" and email "poochprofessionalgrooming@gmail.com" beneath in body
      weight, each as a real link (tel: and mailto:). Right column holds opening hours as an
      aligned day/time table — days in muted small-caps, times in ink, hairline rules between
      rows — Monday through Saturday 9:00am–5:00pm, Sunday closed. On mobile the two columns
      stack, address above hours. No map (no embed or coordinates available). A "Get directions"
      text link in primary beneath the address column points to a Google Maps search for
      "3 Misten Avenue, Altona North VIC 3025".

  - id: cta
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Close the homepage with a single clear action. A visitor who has read this far is ready to
      book; do not delay them with further content.
    spec: >
      Quiet-close treatment: a narrow centred block on the ground colour (#fffaf7). One line of
      display text at 2rem: "Ready to treat your pup?" in ink 700-weight. One primary-coloured
      button beneath: "Book online now!" linking to the external booking URL. A secondary text
      link beside or beneath it: "Get a free quote" linking to the quote form. Below both: "Or
      call us: (03) 7057 0538" in muted body type, the number as a tel: link. On mobile the
      button spans the container width. The sticky bottom bar on mobile mirrors this single action
      — primary background (#f07850), "Book online now!" in #fffaf7 700-weight, a thin persistent
      bar above the browser chrome, never obscuring the accessibility widget (bottom-left corner
      is reserved).

avoid:
  - centred hero with three feature cards directly beneath — the most recognisable generated-site shape
  - stock dog photography or any image URL not in the supplied asset list
  - emoji used as structural icons in the rendered UI (they appear in source copy as shorthand; the built page should use proper glyphs or SVG)
  - a "why choose us" grid of bordered icon-boxes — every highlight is already surfaced honestly in the story and team sections
  - numbered 01/02/03 treatment on services that have no meaningful sequence
  - "Submit" as a button label on any form — use "Send your details" or similar
  - any invented price, service, team member, opening hour or review not present in the content JSON
  - social media icons in the nav or footer — no social URLs are available
  - a map embed or map placeholder image — coordinates and mapEmbed are both null/empty; a placeholder is fabricated content
  - urgency language ("limited spots!", "book before it's too late") — the offers section carries exactly what the business actually states, nothing more
